free_tier.stated: 100 emails per day and 3,000 emails per month on the Email API Free plan, up to 1,000 contacts, at USD 0 with no card
free_tier.notes: The daily limit resets every day and unused sends do not carry over. Each attachment counts as one more email against the daily limit, so a message with one attachment uses 2 of the 100. The Free plan keeps 3 days of logs and allows single address verification only. Email API and Email Marketing are separate accounts. The cheapest paid Email API plan is USD 19 per month for 50,000 emails, and paid plans have no daily limit.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated; each attachment counts as one more email against the daily limit

retention.stated: 3 days of log history on the Free plan, against 7 days on Pro

interface_detail: SMTP at smtp.elasticemail.com on ports 25, 2525, 587 and 465 with TLS 1.2, and the HTTP REST API; the interface vocabulary has no smtp term
tooling: any SMTP client, or curl and the official API libraries against the REST API
chaining: an outbound sender at 100 a day that pairs with an inbound router such as Cloudflare Email Routing for the receiving half; the daily count is the scarce link.

limits.value: 100 emails per day, resetting daily with no carry-over; each attachment counts as one more email
the account must be verified before it can send, and a verified domain set as the default sender is required from the start

limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 1,000 contacts on the Free plan. SMTP accepts 20 concurrent requests from a single IP.

identity_cost.detail: The Email API signup form asks for an email, a password, a first and last name and a field labelled Address, behind a reCAPTCHA, and offers Google sign-in; it has no card field, and the email is confirmed. A profile survey then asks for accurate information about the primary person and organization behind the account, and the account must be verified before it can send; whether that verification asks for a phone number is unverified: behind a sign-up. A domain the sender owns must be verified from the start (SPF mandatory, DKIM encouraged, a tracking CNAME and DMARC recommended); domains of free providers such as gmail.com cannot be verified, and on the Free plan an added domain cannot be removed from the account.

reliability_note: an account placed Under Review has delivery paused; mail submitted meanwhile is queued and sent if the account is reactivated
